q-93093.name: Question 1
q-93093.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
\sqrt[4]{7x+11}+3=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{7x+11}+3 & =0 \\ \sqrt[4]{7x+11} & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

This equation does not have any solutions since its left-hand side is always nonnegative, while the right-hand side is negative.

Therefore, $f(x)$ has no root.

q-102534.name: Question 2
q-102534.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
\sqrt[5]{17-2x}+3=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[5]{17-2x}+3 & =0 \\ \sqrt[5]{17-2x} & =-3 \\ (\sqrt[5]{17-2x})^{5} & =(-3)^{5} \\ 17-2x & =-243 \\ -2x & =-260 \\ x & =130\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=130.$

q-102549.name: Question 3
q-102549.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
5\sqrt[4]{4x+17}-15=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\sqrt[4]{4x+17}-15 & =0 \\ 5\sqrt[4]{4x+17} & =15 \\ \sqrt[4]{4x+17} & =3 \\ (\sqrt[4]{4x+17})^{4} & ={3}^{4} \\ 4x+17 & =81 \\ 4x & =64 \\ x & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\sqrt[4]{4\cdot 16+17}-15 & =0 \\ 5\sqrt[4]{81}-15 & =0 \\ 5\cdot 3-15 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=16.$
